chip.description: SPC700-core sound processor of the SNES: the CPU core plus three timers (two clocked at 8 kHz, one at 64 kHz), four bidirectional main-CPU communication ports and a 64-byte IPL boot ROM, executing from external RAM.
chip.notes: src/devices/machine/s_smp.cpp in MAME 0.288, device full name "Nintendo/Sony S-SMP": a 0x40-byte "sound_ipl" ROM region, four m_port_in/m_port_out registers, and three timer channels of which "if timer channel is 0 or 1 we update at 64000/8". Filed cpu under taxonomy TB2: the device carries no RAM region of its own and the 64-byte IPL ROM is a bootstrap rather than the program store, so the part fetches its program from external memory. Manufacturer recorded as Sony, which designed the SPC700 core; MAME attributes the part to "Nintendo/Sony" and the dataset cannot express two manufacturers on one row.
